sub_strands.values: Respect:is developed as the learner appreciates diverse opinions from peers during discussions on whether the predictions made are accurate.
sub_strands.pcis: Environmental Education: This is promoted as the learner is sensitised on how to use resources properly through texts and stories read.
sub_strands.links: The learner can apply comprehension skills when reading texts in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: identify wordsthat have the target sounds /l/, /r/ and /s/ from a text related to the theme
make predictions about a story using the title and the pictures
respond to direct and indirect questions from a text to show comprehension
adopt reading pictures and textsfor enjoyment and information

learning_experiences: listen to a short dialogue from an audio recording,
pick out interjections of surprise from the dialogue,
make different familiar faces showing surprise,
read out sentence structures containing interjections ofsurprise from a story, poem or conversation they have listened to,
work jointly to role play the interjections of surprise as modelled by peers, the teacher or from a video recording,
search for emojis showing surprise from digital texts,
constructsentences using interjections of surprise,
recite rhymes and poems featuring interjections of surprise.
key_inquiry_questions: How do people show surprise?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy: The learner’s interaction with digital technology is enhanced as they use digital devices to search for emojis showing surprise.
Communication: The learner’s ability to write clearly and correctly is developed as they use interjections of surprise in simple sentences.
sub_strands.values: Unity: This is reinforced as the learner works collaboratively with peers to role play the interjections of surprise as modelled by peers, the teacher or from a video recording.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as they use interjections correctly in communication.
sub_strands.links: The learner can use the knowledge on interjections of surprise to learn similar concepts in Kiswahili Language and Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: identify words showing surprise from a text
use words showing surprise in simple sentences
adopt the use of interjections of surprise in day-to-day communication

learning_experiences: circle words showing colour, height, feelings, taste, and smell, among others,
team up to create a list of words describing people, things, and places,
copy sentences featuring common descriptive words (adjectives),
write dictated words,
match pictures with the correct sentences,
form five-word sentences using descriptive words,
fill in gaps with the correct descriptive word.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are words important in writing?
sub_strands.core_competences: be developed: Communication: The learner’s ability to write clearly and correctly is developed as they write sentences of not more than five words.
sub_strands.values: Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as the learner displays a team spirit as they work with peers to create a list of words describing people, things, and places.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills (Self-esteem): The learner acquires a greater level of self-esteem as they express himself/herself creatively in writing.
sub_strands.links: The learner can apply writing skills to write correctly in other learning areas.

outcomes.text: pick out words describing people, things, and places from a text
write short sentences related to the theme using descriptive words
realise the importance of writing correct and meaningful sentences to express meaning
